newsitem.title: UK: Compaq sees '97 Europe PC strength.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sees '97 Europe PC strength.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent

Sales of personal computers will continue their strong growth in Europe in 1997, despite recent news pointing to weakness in the biggest market, Germany, a senior executive of Compaq Computer Corp told a press conference on Tuesday.

"What we are seeing now is an improving economic situation and that will help produce market sales better than 1996," said Andreas Barth Barth, Compaq's Senior Vice-President, and General Manager for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Last week's news that German unemployment had risen to its highest level since 1933 sent shudders through financial markets. Other European countries have been slashing spending as they strive to meet the conditions for European monetary union in 1999.
Some experts believe this will have a deflationary impact on economies, and not least force governemts to cut back spending on information technology.
"Last year Germany was weaker, France and Scandinavia (were) weaker, but improvements in the market place, and with our full range of products, we are positive about good growth in 1997," Barth said.
He said growth in the personal computer and server markets in western Europe would improve 14 percent in 1997, up from 10 percent last year. This compares with a powerful 25 percent growth in 1995.
Barth was asked how he reconciled this improved growth forecast with fragile economic conditions across much of Europe.

"All the forecasts we see are showing better conditions, improving investment. You can question this and wonder if they are correct or not. But these problems (like German unemployment) are structural problems. A lot of companies are reengineering so they need to invest in IT," Barth said.

According to Compaq, the world's leading seller of personal computers, spending on information technology generally in western Europe will rise 15 percent in 1997, up from 1996's $61 billion. And the pace will be even more torrid in eastern Europe - up 28 percent from $6 billion.

Compaq is the personal computer market leader in Europe with 12.4 percent of the market last year, selling more than two million, according to market researcher CONTEXT. This puts it way ahead of International Business Machines Corp's 9.7 percent, and third placed Hewlett-Packard's 5.4 percent.
Eckhard Pfeiffer, President and Chief Executive Officer of Houston, Texas based Compaq, said the company's improved profitability in 1996 was helped by more efficient handling of stocks.
"This (inventory move) allowed a dramatic improvement in our balance sheet, and there's a lot more to come in 1997," Pfeiffer said in speech.
Compaq's revenues last year hit $18.1 billion and earnings were $1.3 billion, compared with $14.8 billion and $789 million in 1995.
He reitterated the company's ambition to notch up revenues of $40 billion by 2000, representing a compound annual growth rate of 25 percent from 1996.
"1997 will again show pretty good growth - about 20 percent for desktops, and even higher 25 percent for portables," Pfeiffer said.

Answering questions, Pfeiffer said the market for personal computers in China was burgeoning - sales would double this year to two million overall. But he said that although sales were accelerating, trading conditions were tough.
"Also Asia in general is quite strong, better than Europe, and we anticipate 20 percent or so (growth) this year," Pfeiffer said.
